title: Chapter III

teacherSummary.text: Nick receives a formal invitation to one of Gatsby's parties, where hundreds of uninvited guests drink, dance and gossip about the host. With Jordan he meets the owl-eyed man in the library, amazed that the books are real. Nick talks with a young man who turns out to be Gatsby, with his reassuring smile and 'old sport.' Gatsby speaks privately with Jordan. Leaving, guests see a car wreck in the ditch. Nick describes his own ordinary life and his friendship with Jordan, who lies and is a careless driver.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “It was one of those rare smiles with a quality of eternal reassurance in it” slowly and put it in my own words: Nick describes Gatsby's smile as rare and as giving eternal reassurance. Next, craft. I notice the extreme words "rare" and "eternal," which make the smile sound almost magical. The strongest word is “reassurance”: it means comfort that you are believed in, exactly what Nick feels. Then, effect. What does Gatsby's smile do to the person who receives it? My answer: Gatsby's smile makes the person who receives it feel understood and believed in; Nick is drawn in, and we see how Gatsby can create the image people want.

contentNotes.teacherNote: Gatsby's party runs on illegal alcohol, and a drunk guest wrecks a car (the wheel comes off). Give Prohibition context and discuss impaired driving as a real danger, not a joke. Jordan's 'Do you want to commit suicide?' is a flip remark about reckless driving; if students pick it up, note that we say 'die by suicide' and point to support.
